name: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4
route: Applied to the skin in serums and creams
status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
mechanism: Copies a fragment of collagen that, in cultured cells, signals connective-tissue cells to build more collagen and fibronectin

article.summary: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (Matrixyl) is a skincare peptide designed to stimulate collagen. One 12-week placebo-controlled trial showed fewer visible wrinkles; other evidence is limited.
article.takeaway: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4, sold as Matrixyl, is a short chain of five amino acids (KTTKS) with a fatty acid attached. KTTKS copies a fragment of type I collagen that, in cultured cells, prompted connective-tissue cells to make more collagen and fibronectin.[^1] In a 12-week split-face trial of 93 women, a moisturizer containing it improved wrinkles and fine lines more than the same moisturizer without it.[^2] That is one of very few controlled human studies, so **the evidence is limited**.
glance: Serums and creams, usually once or twice daily
Signal peptide that mimics a collagen fragment
Cell studies and few controlled human trials

blocks.text: Skin gets much of its strength from collagen, a protein made by cells called fibroblasts. When collagen is produced, short pieces are clipped off its ends. Researchers found that one of these pieces, a stretch of five amino acids called KTTKS, boosted collagen and fibronectin output when added to cultured cells.[^1]

Pal-KTTKS is that sequence with palmitic acid, a fatty acid, attached. The fatty tail makes the molecule more oil-friendly and, in theory, better at entering skin. The idea is that skin reads the fragment as a sign of breakdown and builds more structure in response. This mechanism is mainly shown in a dish, not in living human skin.

rows: KTTKS was the smallest sequence that stimulated collagen and fibronectin production in several kinds of connective-tissue cells[^1]
A moisturizer with 3 ppm pal-KTTKS beat the plain moisturizer for wrinkles and fine lines on imaging analysis and expert grading[^2]
At roughly 800 daltons it is well above the 500-dalton size usually seen as the limit for easy skin absorption, though the fatty chain may help[^3]

blocks.text: A systematic review of over-the-counter anti-aging ingredients concluded that good supporting data are often missing.[^4] Larger, longer and independent trials of this peptide would be needed to know how much it matters.

Pal-KTTKS is a common ingredient in serums, eye creams and moisturizers, often alongside other peptides, vitamin C or hyaluronic acid. Products are typically applied once or twice a day. The trial judged results after 12 weeks, so any change is likely to take months, not days.[^2] Labels seldom state how much active peptide a product holds, which makes a store-bought cream hard to compare with the one that was tested.

The peptide was well tolerated on the skin in the 12-week trial.[^2] A 2026 paper that screened cosmetic peptides with computer-based tools found that pal-KTTKS resembles skin structural proteins and lacked the toxin-like features of known harmful peptides; that is a screening method, not a human safety study.[^5] As with any cosmetic, irritation or allergy can come from other ingredients in the formula.

Cosmetics do not need FDA approval before sale, and a product that claims to change how skin works can be treated as a drug.[^6] Since 2022, companies must keep safety records and report serious adverse events to FDA within 15 business days.[^7]

Pal-KTTKS has a sensible rationale, cell data and at least one controlled trial showing modest wrinkle improvement. It is a low-risk ingredient to find in a moisturizer, but it is not a substitute for daily sunscreen or for prescription treatments with a longer research record.

evidence.label: Limited: one controlled trial plus lab data
evidence.text: The best human evidence is a single 12-week split-face trial that found a benefit at a very low concentration.[^2] Mechanism data come mainly from cell culture,[^1] and broader reviews describe good evidence for cosmetic anti-aging ingredients as often lacking.[^4]

faq.q: Is Matrixyl the same as retinol?
faq.a: No. Retinol is a vitamin A derivative that acts on retinoid receptors in skin cells. Pal-KTTKS is a peptide thought to act as a collagen-building signal, and it has much less clinical research behind it.

faq.q: How long does it take to see results?
faq.a: The trial measured results after 12 weeks of use.[^2] The studies cited here do not show how long any benefit lasts after stopping.

faq.q: Can a peptide cream really reach collagen deep in the skin?
faq.a: That is uncertain. At about 800 daltons it is larger than the 500-dalton rule of thumb for skin absorption,[^3] and no skin-depth data for this specific peptide in people were found among the sources reviewed.
